clue.text: Clears bed's clothes after a loss

definitions.meaning: to clear a garden bed of unwanted plants is to pull them out, a verb sense
widow's ... are the black mourning clothes worn after a bereavement

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away the clothes on a bed after a loss, perhaps a bereavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' reads as furniture but is a flowerbed; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener uproots weeds to clear a flowerbed, and widow's weeds are traditional mourning garments.

clue.text: Someone in church with proper wish to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchgoer has a sincere desire to mend their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges PROPER WISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper is one attending a religious service, praying in a congregation.

clue.text: Starter of escalope Cliff obtained that may be served in bistro

definitions.text: that may be served in bistro

indicators.note: starter means the opening letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff
got means obtained

explanation.surface: A diner orders veal escalope as a starter at a French bistro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a course on the menu but signals the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in garlic butter are a classic French dish served in bistros.

clue.text: Maybe bar contains nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the word before go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A bar of chocolate perhaps contains nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like an ingredient but rearranges CONTAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction can be a penalty or prohibition, so a bar or embargo is one example.

clue.text: Misleadingly articulate girl goes to gallery

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman
the Tate is the well-known London art gallery

explanation.surface: An eloquent young woman heads off to an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misleadingly articulate' looks like an adverb on an adjective but is a verb phrase: to articulate misleadingly. The TATE is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstate something is to express it wrongly or deceptively, putting it falsely into words.

clue.text: The rise of James Anderson

indicators.note: of means the letters are taken from within the following name

explanation.surface: A sports story about the career rise of the England bowler James Anderson.
explanation.walkthrough: James Anderson is a famous English fast bowler, irrelevant except for his letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill, an elevated landform rising above the plain.

clue.text: Games being taken up gives sharper edge

indicators.note: in a down light taken up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: sports are games

explanation.surface: Taking up sports gives one a competitive edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken up' reads SPORTS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To strop a razor is to sharpen it on a leather strap, honing its blade.

clue.text: Part of jacket seen on an independent fashion designer

parts.note: an arm is a sleeve, part of a jacket

explanation.surface: A detail on a jacket shows it to be by an independent designer.
explanation.walkthrough: Giorgio Armani is the Italian fashion designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giorgio Armani is a celebrated Italian couturier who founded a famous fashion house.

clue.text: Nick's advantage

definitions.meaning: in cricket a nick is a thin touch off the side of the bat
a slight superiority over a rival, as in having the upper hand

explanation.surface: Somebody called Nick holds an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name; it is the verb or noun for a slight cut or a snick in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman who nicks the ball gets an edge, and an edge is also a competitive lead.

clue.text: French author's second risque character

parts.note: Jean Racine was a French playwright; his name with the possessive gives the letters plus S

explanation.surface: A French writer's second character is rather saucy.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's of 'author's' is kept as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Raciness is the quality of being suggestive or slightly indecent, a risque nature.

clue.text: Press for a meeting about war hero admitting nothing

indicators.note: about means the word for meeting goes round what follows

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

indicators.note: admitting means the war hero's letters take in the zero inside them

parts.note: a VC (Victoria Cross holder) is a decorated war hero
O is the zero shape, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A press campaign for a reunion about a war hero who admits nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Victoria Cross is Britain's top gallantry award, so its holder is a war hero; 'about' and 'admitting' nest one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to argue publicly in favour of something, to campaign or lobby for it.

clue.text: Money off record released around November

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: around means the released word goes round the November letter

parts.note: out means released, as from prison
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A record is released in November at a reduced price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A discount is a reduction in price, an amount taken off the cost.

clue.text: That woman's name recalled one with unorthodox views

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning belonging to that woman

indicators.note: recalled, called back, means the word for name is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A woman's name is remembered as belonging to a dissenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns CITE to ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds beliefs contrary to established religious or orthodox doctrine; a dissenter.

clue.text: Lower undergarments — bloomers

parts.note: a cow is something that lows, or moos
slips are women's undergarments

explanation.surface: Lowering one's undergarments to reveal bloomers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is one that lows (moos), and 'bloomers' are not knickers but flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowslips are wild yellow spring flowers, so they are plants that bloom.

clue.text: Infatuation shown by part of conference, say, supporting old boy

indicators.note: in a down light the lower part supports, here in an across the second piece is placed after, holding up the first

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a session is one sitting of a conference, an example of a part

explanation.surface: A former pupil's crush is on show at a conference session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' places the second piece after the old boy; 'say' flags the conference part as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a compulsive fixation, much like an infatuation that dominates someone's thoughts.

clue.text: Flask placed in bag at the bottom

indicators.note: placed in means the flask's letters go inside the bag's

parts.note: to net is to bag or catch; a net is also a bag
a Thermos is a vacuum flask

explanation.surface: A flask is put in the bottom of a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: Thermos is a brand name that has become a generic word for a vacuum flask.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest, the furthest down of all, so it is at the bottom.

clue.text: What one must do to get into Oxford? Commit a faux pas

definitions.text: What one must do to get into Oxford?
definitions.meaning: an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe, so you must insert a foot to wear it
to make an embarrassing blunder or social gaffe

explanation.surface: A question about university admission, then a warning about blundering.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford here is not the university but an Oxford shoe, a laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to say or do something tactless, blundering into an awkward social mistake.

clue.text: Rhythm really oddly unspiritual

parts.note: tempo is the speed or rhythm of music

indicators.note: oddly means the letters in odd positions of the following word are taken

explanation.surface: Music with a really odd rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of 'really'.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporal means of worldly or secular affairs rather than spiritual or religious matters.

clue.text: Oil-bearing region on earth's being developed

indicators.note: developed means worked into new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An oilfield somewhere on earth is being developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being developed' rearranges ON EARTHS, the 's counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea between Britain and Scandinavia holds major offshore oil fields.

clue.text: Left-winger may take such editing

parts.note: a red is a communist or socialist, a left-winger
action is what one may take, as in the phrase take action

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist might take part in such editing of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may take such' points to ACTION via the phrase 'take action'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redaction is the editing or censoring of a text, blacking out passages before release.

clue.text: Party — wise to get amount of drug?

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
sage means wise

explanation.surface: Is it wise to go to a party to get hold of drugs?
explanation.definitionFit: A dosage is the measured quantity of medicine to be taken at one time.

clue.text: Minister's assistant and copper going over charge

indicators.note: in a down light going over means sitting on top, so the copper letters come first

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A government minister's aide and a policeman go over a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' is a clergyman, not a politician; 'copper' looks like a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate assists a parish priest or vicar, a clergyman serving as a helper.

clue.text: Source of better advice, priest gets conversion after time

indicators.note: after means the converted letters come behind the time letter
conversion means the letters of priest are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A priest dispenses advice about conversion, given in good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not an adjective; 'conversion' rearranges the clergyman's letters to give IPSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster gives racing or betting tips to gamblers, so is a source of advice to punters.

clue.text: Spray disease of plant that's suspect

parts.note: a mist is a fine spray of liquid
rust is a fungal disease of plants

explanation.surface: A gardener sprays a plant suffering from a suspicious disease.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust someone is to doubt or be wary of them, to regard them as suspect.

clue.text: Assemble for service

definitions.meaning: to gather together in large numbers, as crowds do
the Eucharist celebrated in Catholic churches

explanation.definitionFit: Crowds amass when they gather together, and Mass is the Catholic eucharistic church service.

clue.text: Follow story as told

indicators.note: as told means as spoken out loud, so the word's sound is used

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Follow the story as it is told.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow or track them secretly, like a detective.

clue.text: Clears of building, getting outside

indicators.note: building means the letters of the fodder are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A building is cleared of things, which are put outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges the letters of CLEARS OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfresco means in the open air, so eating outside is dining alfresco.

clue.text: Wicked woman cast off vice

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin
evil is wickedness, a vice

explanation.surface: A wicked woman throws off her vices.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a cruel, malicious woman, a female fiend.

clue.text: Was inclined to make fast time covering area

indicators.note: covering means the fasting season's letters go over and around the area letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: Someone was inclined to make good time while covering ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make fast time' suggests speed, but fast is fasting; 'to make' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, meaning was disposed or tended towards something.
